lesson.title: Blending Traits: When Pink Snapdragons Break Mendel's Rules
lesson.summary: In incomplete dominance, neither allele fully masks the other, so the heterozygote displays a brand new, intermediate phenotype rather than simply looking like the dominant homozygote.
lesson.body:
The monohybrid crosses covered earlier all assumed complete dominance, where a heterozygote looks identical to the homozygous dominant individual because one allele fully masks the other. That assumption does not always hold. In incomplete dominance, the heterozygote's phenotype falls in between the two homozygous phenotypes instead of matching either one.

Snapdragon flower color is a textbook example. Cross a plant with red flowers, genotype C-R C-R, with a plant that has white flowers, genotype C-W C-W. Every offspring in that first generation has pink flowers, genotype C-R C-W. The heterozygote is not red hiding a recessive white allele, it is a genuinely new, intermediate color, because a single copy of the red-pigment allele only produces about half the normal amount of pigment, not enough to look fully red.

Now cross two of those pink offspring together, C-R C-W by C-R C-W. Each parent produces C-R and C-W gametes in equal proportion, so the resulting offspring come out as one quarter C-R C-R, red, one half C-R C-W, pink, and one quarter C-W C-W, white. The genotype ratio is the familiar one to two to one, but here the phenotype ratio matches it exactly, one red to two pink to one white, because every genotype now corresponds to its own distinct, visible phenotype rather than two genotypes collapsing into one dominant look.

That exact match between genotype ratio and phenotype ratio is the practical signal of incomplete dominance, and it is a useful thing to check for in any unfamiliar cross. It contrasts with ordinary dominance, where a 1:2:1 genotype ratio hides behind a 3:1 phenotype ratio. It also looks superficially similar to another exception covered next, codominance, but the two are different mechanisms that happen to produce similar looking math.
